tldr: Democrats swept the House and Senate in the Nov 3 midterms -- confirmed overnight as the clean catalyst behind Wednesday's huge relief rally: VIX crashed -20.3% to 16.61, Dow +3.03% (best post-midterm day since 1982), S&P +1.58%.

Gold and silver rallied hard in parallel (+3.3%/+5.5%) on dollar weakness and fiscal-hedging, with miners (NEM +9.9%, HL +13.2%) confirming broad participation -- the best session in months for the levered-silver leg of this book, though reporting flags metals are still trading correlated to equity deleveraging, not as a clean hedge.

Oil kept falling (Brent -8.7%, WTI -8.4%) on Iran-de-escalation bets even as a bullish EIA inventory draw printed -- a genuine two-sided setup, not a settled call, with Treasury Sec. Bessent saying 'the world can live without Iranian oil.'

Underneath the rally, two hawkish-skeptic threads persist: CME FedWatch's December hike odds firmed to ~81% on sticky ISM Services prices-paid, and Oracle's CDS sits near record levels (S&P downgrade to BBB-) alongside Meta's record 114.79bp -- AI-capex credit stress hasn't gone away.
Trump's Forbes-estimated net worth fell ~$168M to ~$6.4B as Trump Media (DJT) plunged ~25% to a new all-time low on the same midterm result -- a market-driven move, not a new disclosure.

China's rare-earth export truce (Announcement No. 70) is reported extended to Jan 10 2027 after the Trump-Xi summit, but Beijing has not published matching legal text before the original Nov 10 deadline -- still the highest-conviction near-term catalyst for the MP/Lynas/UUUU/USAR watchlist, and MP reports Q3 earnings today.

Market: Fear & Greed jumped to 31/Fear from 19/Extreme Fear; breadth broadened on the day itself (advancers led ~2.6:1) though slower-moving gauges (52wk highs/lows, 50-DMA breadth) haven't caught up; global fund flows still stuck on the week-ending-Oct-28 cut, next due Nov 5-6.

Flows-investors: Korea rolled forward to Nov 4 (a V-shaped reversal -- domestic institutions and retail absorbed heavy foreign selling); Hong Kong Southbound swung to -HK$32.8bn after Nov 3's six-month-high buy; Japan/Singapore/US carried forward with documented data gaps.

regime.label: Election-clarity relief rally vs. sticky-inflation hike risk
regime.oneLiner: A confirmed Democratic sweep of Congress cleared election-uncertainty hedging and crushed the VIX, but firming ~81% December-hike odds and record AI-capex credit stress (Oracle, Meta CDS) mean the rally sits on top of unresolved risk, not past it.

topNews.headline: Democrats sweep House and Senate in US midterms, ending divided-government uncertainty
topNews.actionable: Removal of election-outcome uncertainty was the single biggest catalyst behind Wednesday's broad risk-on move, including the gold/silver/miners leg of this portfolio, and sets up a gridlock narrative that markets are reading as policy-predictable rather than destabilizing.

topNews.headline: VIX crashes 20% as Wall Street posts biggest post-midterm rally in 44 years
topNews.actionable: The volatility collapse confirms the midterm result is being priced as a de-risking event, not a new source of policy shock, which argues for holding through Fed/BOE/NFP catalysts this week rather than hedging into them.

topNews.headline: Gold vaults back above $4,000 and silver jumps to $52.49 as dollar and yields drop post-election
topNews.actionable: This is the direct driver of the GDX/SILJ/HL/NEM leg of the portfolio's best day in months; record ETF inflows suggest the move has institutional participation rather than being purely a short-covering spike, supporting continued long exposure.

topNews.headline: Oil extends slide below $100 Brent as Iran reopens door to Hormuz deal and Trump plays down new strikes
topNews.actionable: No direct oil holdings in the portfolio, but a de-escalating Hormuz risk premium removes a tail-risk input into the macro backdrop and supports the broader risk-on tone benefiting equities/miners; watch for any reversal if Hormuz talks stall again before the Nov 10 rare-earth truce deadline.

topNews.headline: China's rare-earth export truce, due to expire Nov 10, reportedly extended to Jan 10 2027 after Trump-Xi summit -- but Beijing hasn't published matching legal text
topNews.actionable: If the extension holds, it reduces near-term supply-shock risk for SMIC/Xiaomi and global tech, which is incrementally bearish for the US/allied rare-earth buildout thesis (MP/Lynas/Energy Fuels/USA Rare Earth) that trades on China-decoupling urgency -- watch Nov 10 closely for whether Beijing actually codifies the extension or lets it lapse.

signals: GLD: the model's clearest bullish lean this run (pUp3m 0.63, confidence 0.55), consistent with Wednesday's dollar-weakness/fiscal-hedging gold surge to $4,072 -- consider watching for follow-through vs. a reversal if Friday's NFP beats and re-ignites the Dec-hike case.

XLE: the model's clearest bearish lean (pUp3m 0.40, confidence 0.55), as Wednesday's Iran-de-escalation bets crushed Brent/WTI another ~8% even against a bullish EIA draw -- watch for confirmation or a stall on fresh Hormuz headlines.

MP Materials reports Q3 earnings after today's close with 20%+ short interest and a Pentagon-subsidy-dependency debate live -- the rare-earth basket's most binary single-name risk this week (model pUp3m 0.48, confidence 0.45).

MU: Congress (Rep. McGuire), Soros Fund Management and a broad ETF-flow base all leaned into the AI-memory trade the same week -- then MU fell sharply Nov 4 anyway, worth watching as a reminder that convergence isn't protection.

SMCI: a genuine beat-and-raise quarter (FY27 revenue guidance raised to $72-82B) landed on top of concentrated hedge-fund ownership and heavy retail chatter -- the cleanest three-way signal convergence this run, worth watching for follow-through.
